Microsoft Phone Link Not Showing Messages on Windows 11? Fix It

By
Emiley
-
September 9, 2026
Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft Phone Link allows users to access phone features like messages and notifications on a Windows PC, but after a Windows update, some users find that it stops showing messages. This issue can result from app updates, permissions changes, network issues, or communication problems between the phone app and PC app.
  • To resolve Microsoft Phone Link issues after a Windows update, users can try several fixes including restarting both devices, updating both the Phone Link app on the PC and the Link to Windows app on the phone, repairing the app via Windows Settings, and ensuring all necessary permissions are granted on the phone.

Microsoft Phone Link is one of the easiest ways to access phone messages, notifications, calls, photos, and other mobile features directly from a Windows PC. However, some users find that Microsoft Phone Link is not opening or showing messages after a Windows update, even though the app worked normally before the update.

The problem can appear in several ways. Phone Link may briefly open and immediately close, remain stuck on the loading screen, show your phone as disconnected, or open normally while refusing to sync recent SMS messages. In most cases, you do not need to roll back Windows or completely reset your PC.

This guide covers the most useful fixes for Phone Link issues on Windows 11 and Windows 10, including app repair, permissions, synchronization, Microsoft Store updates, device relinking, and more advanced recovery options.

Why Is Microsoft Phone Link Not Working After a Windows Update?

Phone Link depends on several components working together. These include the Windows Phone Link app, Microsoft’s cross-device services, your Microsoft account, network connectivity, and the Link to Windows app installed on your phone.

A Windows update can occasionally leave one of these components in an inconsistent state. The update itself is not necessarily defective. The problem may simply be caused by cached Phone Link data or an older version of the mobile app that no longer communicates correctly with the updated Windows component.

Common reasons include:

  • Corrupted Phone Link app data after an update
  • An outdated version of Phone Link
  • An outdated Link to Windows app on the phone
  • SMS, notification, contacts, or background permissions being removed
  • Microsoft account synchronization problems
  • Battery Saver stopping background synchronization
  • Android battery optimization restricting Link to Windows
  • A broken phone-to-PC pairing
  • Temporary Microsoft Store app problems
  • Network or Wi-Fi isolation preventing communication

The best approach is to start with the least disruptive fixes and only reset or relink the app if basic troubleshooting does not work.

1. Restart Both Your Windows PC and Phone

Start with a proper restart of both devices, particularly if Phone Link stopped working immediately after installing a Windows update.

On Windows, select Start > Power > Restart. Avoid simply putting the computer to sleep and waking it again. A restart reloads Windows services and cross-device components that may still be using files from before the update.

Restart your Android phone or iPhone as well. Once both devices are running again, wait until they have connected to Wi-Fi and then launch Phone Link.

If the app opens but messages are still missing, continue with the next methods.

2. Update Microsoft Phone Link

Windows Update and Microsoft Store app updates are handled separately. This means you can install the newest Windows update while still having an older version of Phone Link installed.

Open Microsoft Store and go to Library. Check for available app updates and install any update available for Phone Link.

If Phone Link itself opens, you can also check its update status from the app’s settings. Microsoft recommends keeping Phone Link and Link to Windows on their latest available versions because newer app releases include compatibility and synchronization fixes.

After installing the update, close Phone Link completely and open it again.

3. Update Link to Windows on Your Phone

Do not update only the Windows side. The Link to Windows app running on your phone also needs to be compatible with the version of Phone Link installed on your PC.

On Android

Open the Link to Windows app and check its settings for updates. You can also update it through Google Play. On supported Samsung devices where Link to Windows is built into the operating system, an update may be available through Google Play or Galaxy Store.

After updating the app, restart Link to Windows and reopen Phone Link on the PC.

This is especially important if Phone Link displays an Update Required message or your phone suddenly appears offline after updating Windows.

4. Repair Phone Link From Windows Settings

If Phone Link is not opening after a Windows update, repairing the application is one of the best fixes to try first.

Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps. Find Phone Link, open its options, and select Advanced options.

Scroll down and select Repair.

The Repair option attempts to fix damaged app files without deleting your Phone Link data or completely removing the connection with your phone. This makes it safer to try before performing a full reset.

Once Windows finishes repairing the application, launch Phone Link again.

5. Reset Phone Link If It Still Will Not Open

If repairing Phone Link does not help, return to Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Phone Link > Advanced options and select Reset.

Resetting is more aggressive than repairing. Windows clears Phone Link’s local application data and restores the app to its default state.

You may need to sign back into your Microsoft account or reconnect your phone afterward.

This method is particularly useful when Phone Link opens for a second and immediately closes, remains stuck on its startup screen, or stopped loading after Windows Update.

6. Check Phone Link Mobile Device Settings in Windows 11

Recent versions of Windows 11 provide additional mobile-device controls outside the Phone Link application itself.

Go to Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Mobile devices. Make sure Allow this PC to access your mobile devices or a similarly named mobile-device access option is enabled.

If your phone appears under the connected devices list, confirm that it is enabled and correctly associated with your Microsoft account.

This matters because newer Windows cross-device features can share the same phone connection used by Phone Link. A broken or disabled mobile-device connection can therefore cause Phone Link to show your device as unavailable.

7. Fix Phone Link Not Showing Messages

If Phone Link opens normally but messages are not showing, the problem is usually synchronization or permissions rather than the Windows application itself.

First, make sure your phone has an active internet connection. Open Link to Windows and confirm that your PC still appears as a connected or linked device.

Then send a new SMS message to your phone or ask someone to send one. Open the Messages section of Phone Link and give it a moment to synchronize.

If older messages appear but new messages do not, check the permissions described below.

8. Restore Link to Windows Permissions on Android

Android permissions can sometimes change after app updates, operating system updates, security changes, or extended periods of inactivity.

Open Settings > Apps > Link to Windows > Permissions on your Android phone. The exact menu names differ slightly between Samsung, Google Pixel, OnePlus, Xiaomi, Motorola, and other manufacturers.

Allow the permissions required for the Phone Link features you use. Depending on your phone and Android version, these can include access related to:

  • SMS or messages
  • Contacts
  • Phone or calls
  • Photos and media
  • Nearby devices
  • Notifications

You should only grant permissions required for the Phone Link features you intend to use.

After changing the permissions, reopen Link to Windows and Phone Link.

9. Disable Battery Optimization for Link to Windows

Android battery optimization is a common reason Phone Link works when initially opened but stops syncing after the phone has been idle.

Go to your Android phone’s Settings > Apps > Link to Windows > Battery. Look for an option such as Unrestricted, Don’t optimize, or Allow background activity.

The exact wording depends on the phone manufacturer.

Allowing Link to Windows to run in the background prevents Android from aggressively suspending the connection when the screen is off.

You should also temporarily turn off Battery Saver on your Windows laptop while testing Phone Link because Windows power-saving settings can interfere with background synchronization and notifications.

10. Reset Notification Access for Link to Windows

If messages work but Phone Link notifications have disappeared, reset the Android notification-access permission.

On your Android device, open Settings and search for Notification access. Find Link to Windows.

Turn its notification access off, wait a few seconds, and turn it back on. Accept the permission request when Android displays it.

Then open Phone Link and select Notifications. This forces the notification connection to be established again.

Android 15 and newer versions may also hide content classified by Android as sensitive, including some verification codes and security notifications. If only specific sensitive notifications are missing, this can be Android security behavior rather than a Phone Link synchronization failure.

11. Check Whether You Are Using a Supported Messaging App

If Phone Link shows some conversations but not others, check which messaging application your phone uses.

Standard SMS and MMS messages are the most consistently supported. Messages handled entirely by certain third-party messaging platforms may not appear like normal SMS conversations in Phone Link.

RCS functionality can also differ by phone model, messaging application, mobile operator, and region. Microsoft currently provides additional RCS integration for certain supported Samsung configurations, but users should not assume every feature available inside Google Messages or another messaging client will automatically appear in Phone Link.

If regular SMS messages appear correctly but another type of conversation does not, Phone Link itself may be working normally.

12. Check Your Microsoft Account on Both Devices

The Microsoft account used by Phone Link is an important part of the connection between your PC and phone.

Open Link to Windows on your phone and verify which Microsoft account is signed in. Then check the Microsoft account associated with Phone Link on your PC.

If you recently changed your password, enabled additional account security, changed Windows accounts, or switched Microsoft accounts, sign-in authorization may need to be refreshed.

Signing out and signing back in can restore the authentication session, but try the previous fixes first because signing out may require you to pair the devices again.

13. Check Wi-Fi and Network Connectivity

A slow or unstable internet connection can cause delayed message synchronization even though Phone Link appears to be connected.

Make sure both devices have working network connections. Microsoft generally recommends keeping the PC and Android phone on the same Wi-Fi network while troubleshooting.

If Phone Link works on your home Wi-Fi but not on a workplace, hotel, university, or public network, the network itself could be restricting communication between devices.

Some routers provide a feature called AP Isolation, Client Isolation, or Wireless Isolation. When enabled, devices connected to the same Wi-Fi network are prevented from communicating directly with each other.

For a quick test, temporarily connect the devices to another trusted network and check whether Phone Link starts synchronizing again.

14. Unlink and Reconnect Your Phone

If the Windows update appears to have broken the existing pairing, completely relinking the phone can rebuild the connection.

Open Phone Link > Settings > Devices and remove the affected device.

Next, go to Windows Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Mobile devices > Manage devices. If the same phone is still listed there, remove it.

On Android, open Link to Windows, select your Microsoft account, and sign out or unlink the connected PC as appropriate.

If Bluetooth pairing exists, remove the PC from the phone’s Bluetooth settings and remove the phone from Windows Bluetooth settings as well.

Now launch Phone Link and select the option to add a new device. Follow the instructions and scan the QR code when requested.

Relinking takes longer than repairing the app, which is why it should generally be attempted only after the simpler methods fail.

15. Fix Microsoft Store Problems

If Phone Link cannot update through Microsoft Store, the problem may actually be with the Store rather than Phone Link.

Press Windows + R, type wsreset.exe, and press Enter.

Windows will reset the Microsoft Store cache and reopen the Store. Return to the Library section and check for Phone Link updates again.

You should also install pending Windows updates from Settings > Windows Update. A follow-up cumulative update may contain fixes for problems introduced or exposed by an earlier Windows release.

16. Reset Phone Link With PowerShell

If the normal Reset button does not fix the application, advanced users can reset the Phone Link package through PowerShell.

Open Windows PowerShell or Windows Terminal and run it with administrator privileges.

Command: Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.YourPhone | Reset-AppxPackage

The internal Windows package name still uses Microsoft.YourPhone, which comes from the application’s older Your Phone branding.

After the command completes, restart Windows and try opening Phone Link again.

Use this method only after trying the normal Repair and Reset options. There is usually no benefit in jumping directly to PowerShell for a simple message-sync problem.

17. Run DISM and System File Checker

If several built-in Windows applications stopped working after the same update, the problem may be broader than Phone Link.

Open Windows Terminal or Command Prompt as administrator and run:

DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth

After DISM finishes, run:

sfc /scannow

DISM checks the Windows component store, while System File Checker scans protected system files and replaces damaged copies where possible.

Restart the computer afterward and test Phone Link again.

This step is more appropriate when Phone Link, Microsoft Store, Settings, or other Windows components are simultaneously behaving abnormally.

Should You Uninstall the Latest Windows Update?

Usually, no. Rolling back a Windows update should not be the first fix for Microsoft Phone Link problems.

Repairing or resetting Phone Link, updating both applications, restoring permissions, or rebuilding the phone connection solves most app-specific problems without removing security and reliability updates from Windows.

Consider removing a recent Windows update only when several Windows features started failing immediately after the same update and Microsoft has confirmed a problem with that particular release. Before doing so, install any newer cumulative update that may already contain the fix.

Additional Tips to Keep Phone Link Working Reliably

  • Keep Phone Link updated through Microsoft Store.
  • Keep Link to Windows updated on your phone.
  • Do not aggressively restrict Link to Windows background activity.
  • Keep both devices connected to reliable internet connections.
  • Check Android permissions after major phone software updates.
  • Avoid repeatedly unlinking and pairing the phone unless the existing connection is clearly broken.
  • Restart both devices after major Windows or Android updates if synchronization behaves unusually.
  • Check Windows Mobile devices settings if Phone Link suddenly loses access to a previously connected phone.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why is Microsoft Phone Link not opening after a Windows update?

The Phone Link app may have damaged cached data, an incompatible app version, or a broken Windows app registration after an update. Start by updating Phone Link, then use Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Phone Link > Advanced options > Repair. If that does not work, use Reset.

Why is Phone Link connected but not showing messages?

Check Link to Windows permissions on your phone, internet connectivity, background battery restrictions, and whether the messages are regular SMS or MMS messages. Updating both Phone Link and Link to Windows can also fix synchronization problems.

Will resetting Phone Link delete messages from my phone?

No. Resetting the Windows Phone Link application does not delete SMS messages stored on your physical phone. It clears the Phone Link application’s local Windows data, so you may need to reconnect the device afterward.

Why does Phone Link open and immediately close?

This usually points to damaged application data or an app initialization problem. Repair Phone Link first. If the application still crashes immediately, reset the app and restart Windows.

Do my phone and computer need to be on the same Wi-Fi?

Phone Link can use internet connectivity for several synchronization functions, but keeping both devices on the same reliable Wi-Fi network is recommended while troubleshooting. Certain Phone Link capabilities can also have additional connectivity requirements.

Why are notifications missing even though messages work?

Notification synchronization has separate permissions. On Android, search Settings for Notification access, disable Link to Windows notification access, and enable it again. Also check Battery Saver and Android background battery restrictions.

Why are OTP or verification notifications hidden in Phone Link?

Android 15 and newer versions can classify some notifications containing verification codes or other private information as sensitive. Android may prevent their content from being displayed through Phone Link. Check the notification directly on your phone if this occurs.

Does Phone Link support iPhone messages?

Yes, Phone Link provides iPhone integration, but it works differently from Android and has additional limitations. Bluetooth connectivity is especially important for iPhone integration, and not every messaging feature available on the iPhone can be synchronized to Windows.

Should I reinstall Windows if Phone Link is broken?

No. Reinstalling or resetting Windows is excessive for an isolated Phone Link problem. Repairing the app, resetting it, updating the mobile app, checking permissions, and relinking the phone should all be attempted first.

Final Thoughts

If Microsoft Phone Link is not opening or showing messages after a Windows update, start by restarting both devices and updating Phone Link and Link to Windows. Next, repair Phone Link from Windows Settings and check mobile permissions, battery optimization, notification access, and network connectivity.

If the app still refuses to launch, reset Phone Link and rebuild the connection between the PC and phone. PowerShell reset commands, DISM, and System File Checker should be reserved for cases where ordinary app recovery options fail or other Windows applications are also malfunctioning.

For most users, there is no need to uninstall a Windows update or reset the entire computer. Phone Link problems after an update are usually related to application data, permissions, synchronization, or device pairing, all of which can normally be repaired without affecting the rest of Windows.
